readinessDefinitions.TASK_READY: at least one model stack is qualified on at least two structurally distinct task families
readinessDefinitions.MODEL_READY: at least one frozen fixture family is qualified on both sentinel model families
readinessDefinitions.LOCAL_PAIR_READY: both sentinel model families have at least one qualified fixture AND at least two task families are represented overall; supports pair-local mechanism replication only

capitalItems.title: Refuse the graph before you resolve it, then let the nearer declaration win
capitalItems.purpose: resolve the effective policies of every node in an inheritance graph whose edges carry a declared precedence
capitalItems.provenanceNote: derived from the closure, precedence and well-formedness obligations the F-C contract states; not tuned against any model outcome
clauses: validate the whole graph first — every node, and every inherits entry — and refuse an entry that names a node the graph does not define, at any depth
detect a cycle in the inheritance edges, including a node that inherits itself, and refuse the graph rather than resolving it
compute each node's inherited closure before writing any effective policy, so a refusal leaves no partial result
let a node's OWN declaration win over anything it inherits; between two inherited declarations of one name, let the one reached through the EARLIER inherits entry win
treat a repeated inherits entry as the same edge, so it changes neither the effective policies nor the order
emit the nodes so that every parent precedes its children, breaking a tie between ready nodes by the lexicographically smaller id
a node's effective policies contain only policies from its own inherited closure, so two components that share no edge share no policy
applicability: a declared inheritance graph whose edges carry a precedence order and whose closure must be canonical
limitations: does not authorize any command, path or effect beyond the task envelope
advisory guidance only; it cannot widen write scope or allowed commands

capitalItems.title: Normalize first, then let the most specific match win — and refuse a tie
capitalItems.purpose: select the single rule that applies to a request, under a declared specificity order
capitalItems.provenanceNote: derived from the normalization, specificity and ambiguity obligations the F-D contract states; not tuned against any model outcome
clauses: normalize the rule and the request BEFORE matching: trim the surrounding whitespace and compare letters case-insensitively
rank a match by its specificity, not by the order the rules were written in: a rule that names a host outranks one that matches any host, and a literal segment outranks a wildcard one
a wildcard segment matches EXACTLY one non-empty segment — never zero, never more than one, and never across a separator
two rules whose match is identical after normalization are the SAME rule, and are not a tie
refuse a rule set that binds one id to two different matches, rather than choosing between them
when two DIFFERENT rules tie at the highest specificity, refuse the request as ambiguous rather than resolving it by order
applicability: a rule set whose entries carry a declared specificity and whose selection must be canonical
limitations: does not authorize any command, path or effect beyond the task envelope
advisory guidance only; it cannot widen write scope or allowed commands

sourceAnalogues.name: role and permission inheritance resolution
sourceAnalogues.mechanism: validate graph -> detect invalid references/cycles -> compute closure -> apply declared precedence -> canonicalize

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a role that grants a role that grants it back
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: a node whose inheritance edges form a cycle
mechanismCorrespondence.sharedMechanism: cycle detection over the inheritance edges

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a role naming a permission that does not exist
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: an inherits entry naming a node the graph does not define

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a permission granted by a nearer role
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: a policy declared nearer in the inherits list

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: the effective permission set of a role
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: the effective policy set of a node

sourceAnalogues.name: media-type and Accept-header negotiation
sourceAnalogues.mechanism: normalize -> validate -> rank specificity -> resolve ambiguity -> canonicalize

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a media type written in another case or with parameters
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: a rule or request written in another case

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a specific media type outranking a wildcard range
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: a more specific rule outranking a wider one

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: two ranges that match equally well
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: two rules tying at the top specificity

mechanismCorrespondence.sourceStep: a wildcard range that must not span a boundary
mechanismCorrespondence.targetStep: a `*` segment that matches exactly one segment

fixtureManifests.antiOverfitBasis: the six failure classes and the hidden oracle were authored from the F-C contract (closure, declared precedence, well-formedness) BEFORE any R3-A2 baseline run, and were derived from that mechanism rather than from any DeepSeek or GLM failure trace; the fixture is byte-identical to its pre-execution digest
fixtureManifests.heldOutReason: the evaluation model families were KNOWN during construction, so the fixture is not held out from them; the construction model identity is also UNKNOWN, so independence cannot be demonstrated

smokePolicy: no F-C or F-D run on either model before this schedule; plumbing tests use dummy fixtures only; an accidental new-fixture worker run is a protocol deviation and does NOT count toward Nq

retryPolicy.rule: a valid bad model outcome is NEVER retried; an infrastructure-invalid attempt remains visible and is retried only to reach Nq valid runs for that pair
retryPolicy.infrastructureInvalidDefinition: hostFailure or timeout; it is not a model outcome and not a verdict

runBudget.note: infrastructure-invalid attempts are visible and do not consume the valid-run budget, but the valid runs may never exceed 20
